analysis.title: US economy with 3.4% growth in Q3
key_insights: US real GDP grew 3.4% annualized q/q in Q3 2026, in line with expectations (consensus 3.2%, Commerzbank 3.5%) and up from 2.2% in Q2 and 2.5% in Q1.
Private consumption rose 3.8% and business investment in IT was the main driver: equipment +20.9%, intellectual property (including software) +8.4%, total IT spending +23.2%.
AI-related data center construction lifted nonresidential construction by 5.4%. Private nonresidential investment reached a new high as a share of GDP, above the 2000 New Economy bubble peak.
Residential construction fell 3.3%, weighed down by high mortgage rates. Government spending rose 5.3% and inventory restocking added to growth.
Imports rose 19.7% on AI-related intermediate goods sourced from Asia. The wider trade deficit subtracted a good three percentage points from growth (net exports contribution -3.3 points).

Commerzbank expects expansion to continue into 2027 at somewhat slower rates, because financing conditions are less favorable than a few months ago, the AI investment boost is expected to fade, and fiscal stimulus is waning.
The investment plans of the major AI players suggest growth may already have peaked.

September PCE deflator inflation rose to 3.6%, with core at 3.1%. Commerzbank says strong growth casts doubt on a near-term fall in underlying inflation and that the single September hike will hardly be enough.
Commerzbank expects the Fed to raise rates in December and sees a risk that it will not be the last hike.

sector_views.rationale: AI-driven IT spending (+23.2%) and data center construction were the main growth drivers, though the report expects the boost to subside.
Residential investment fell 3.3% in Q3, weighed down by high mortgage rates.

risk_factors: The AI investment boost may have already peaked, based on major AI players' investment plans.
Fiscal stimulus that supported investment early in the year is waning.
Financing conditions are less favorable than a few months ago.
Higher oil prices, restrictive immigration policy and political uncertainty are headwinds.
Inflation is rising and the Fed may hike more than once, with a risk that December is not the last hike.
Residential construction is weak on high mortgage rates.

geopolitical: Increased uncertainty from domestic and international politics is cited as a headwind that the AI boom offset.
More restrictive US immigration policies are cited as a growth headwind.
